title: Linux NFS Server & Client Configuration
description: Configure an NFS server and client to provide, access, test, and persistently mount a shared filesystem. Students will configure NFS exports, firewall services, client discovery, manual and persistent NFS mounts, read/write access, and NFS verification and troubleshooting.

lab_objective.description: By completing this lab, you will learn how to:
objectives: Create and configure an NFS export directory.
Apply and verify NFS export configuration using exportfs.
Configure the firewall for NFS access.
Discover NFS exports from the client.
Verify NFS mounts using mount and findmnt.
Verify NFS filesystem information using df.
Test NFS read and write access.
Configure a persistent NFS mount using /etc/fstab.
Mount an NFS filesystem using its /etc/fstab entry.
Troubleshoot and verify NFS server and client configuration.
scenario: You are working as a Linux Systems Administrator for an organization that needs to provide a centralized shared directory for application and development teams.
The NFS server has been assigned the responsibility of exporting a shared directory to the client.
The NFS client must discover the exported directory, mount it, verify read/write access, and configure the mount to persist after a system reboot.
Your task is to configure the NFS server, configure the NFS client, verify connectivity, test read/write access, and ensure that the NFS mount is persistent.

tasks.title: Verify the NFS Server Hostname
steps: On the NFS server, verify the system hostname.
set hostname to nfs-server
Hint: hostnamectl set-hostname nfs-server ; bash
Confirm that the hostname is nfs-server.

tasks.title: Install NFS Server Packages
steps: On the NFS server, install the 'nfs-utils' package required to provide NFS server functionality.
Use the appropriate package manager for your Linux distribution.

tasks.title: Enable and Start the NFS Server
steps: Enable and start the NFS server service.
Verify that the NFS server service is active and running.

tasks.title: Enable and Start rpcbind
steps: Make sure the rpcbind service is active and enabled on the NFS server.
Verify the status of the rpcbind service.

tasks.title: Create the NFS Export Directory
steps: Create the NFS export directory.
The directory must be named /nfs_share.

tasks.title: Create the Server Test File
steps: Create the file /nfs_share/server_test.txt.
Add the following content to the file:
This is my first NFS share, and I’m excited to learn how to configure and manage an NFS server.

tasks.title: Configure the NFS Export
steps: Add an entry to /etc/exports so that /nfs_share is exported to the NFS client only.
Use the NFS client's IP address rather than allowing unrestricted access from the entire network.
Configure the export options with read/write access, synchronous writes and root on the client retains root privileges over the NFS export.
Hint:
/nfs_share <NFS_CLIENT_IP>(rw,sync,no_root_squash)

tasks.title: Apply the NFS Export Configuration
steps: Apply the NFS export configuration.
Reload or export the configured NFS share without requiring a server reboot.
Hint: exportfs -avr

tasks.title: Verify Active NFS Exports
steps: Display the currently exported filesystems on the NFS server.
Verify that /nfs_share is exported to the correct NFS client.
Confirm that the export configuration is active.
Hint: exportfs -v

tasks.title: Configure the NFS Server Firewall
steps: Configure the NFS server firewall so that NFS clients can access the exported filesystem.
Allow the NFS service through the firewall.
Allow the mountd service through the firewall.
Allow the rpc-bind service through the firewall.
Reload the firewall configuration.
Verify that the required firewall services are allowed.
Hint:
firewall-cmd --add-service=nfs --permanent
firewall-cmd --add-service=mountd --permanent
firewall-cmd --add-service=rpc-bind --permanent
firewall-cmd --reload
firewall-cmd --list-services
You should see nfs mountd rpc-bind.

tasks.title: Set SELinux to Permissive Mode
steps: Set SELinux to permissive mode on the NFS server.
Verify the current SELinux mode.

tasks.title: Verify the NFS Client Hostname
steps: On the NFS client, verify the system hostname.
set hostname to nfs-client
Hint: hostnamectl set-hostname nfs-client ; bash
Confirm that the hostname is nfs-client.

tasks.title: Install NFS Client Packages
steps: On the NFS client, install the nfs-utils package required to mount NFS filesystems.
Use the appropriate package manager for your Linux distribution.

tasks.title: Enable and Start rpcbind on the Client
steps: Make sure the rpcbind service is active and enabled on the NFS client.
Verify the status of the rpcbind service.

tasks.title: Verify Connectivity to the NFS Server
steps: From the NFS client, verify network connectivity to the NFS server by successfully pinging the NFS server's IP address.

tasks.title: Discover the NFS Export
steps: From the NFS client, query the NFS server and verify that the /nfs_share export is available to the client.
Confirm that /nfs_share is exported by the NFS server.
Hint: showmount -e <nfs_server_IP>

tasks.title: Create the Local Mount Point
steps: On the NFS client, create the /mnt/nfs_share directory to serve as the local mount point for the NFS share.

tasks.title: Mount the NFS Share Manually
steps: On the NFS client, manually mount the NFS server's /nfs_share export on the local mount point /mnt/nfs_share.
Hint:
mount <NFS_SERVER_IP>:/nfs_share /mnt/nfs_share

tasks.title: Verify the NFS Mount
steps: Use an appropriate command to confirm that /mnt/nfs_share is mounted successfully.
Verify that the mounted filesystem type is NFS.
Hint: You can use 'df -h' or findmnt /mnt/nfs_share

tasks.title: Verify the Server Test File from the Client
steps: From the NFS client, verify that /mnt/nfs_share/server_test.txt exists and is accessible.
Verify that the file contains the expected content.
Hint:
cd /mnt/nfs_share/
ls -l server_test.txt
cat server_test.txt
cd

tasks.title: Configure a Persistent NFS Mount
steps: Add an entry to /etc/fstab so that the NFS server's /nfs_share export is automatically mounted at /mnt/nfs_share after a system reboot.
Hint:
<NFS_SERVER>:/nfs_share <mount_point> nfs defaults 0 0

tasks.title: Test the /etc/fstab Configuration
steps: Unmount the NFS share.
Use an appropriate command to test the /etc/fstab entry.
Verify that the NFS share mounts successfully without rebooting the system.
Hint:
mount -a

tasks.title: Mount the NFS Filesystem Using /etc/fstab
steps: Unmount the NFS share again.
Use the configuration defined in /etc/fstab to mount the NFS filesystem.
Do not specify the NFS server or export manually on the command line.
Hint:
mount /mnt/nfs_share

tasks.title: Verify the Persistent NFS Mount
steps: Confirm that /mnt/nfs_share is mounted.
Verify that the source of the mount is nfs-server:/nfs_share.
Verify that the filesystem type is NFS.
Hint:
findmnt /mnt/nfs_share

tasks.title: Create and Verify Client Write Access
steps: From the NFS client, create /mnt/nfs_share/client_test.txt to verify that the client has write access to the NFS share.
Add the following content to /mnt/nfs_share/client_test.txt:
This file was created from the NFS client to verify write access to the NFS shared filesystem.
On the NFS server, verify that /nfs_share/client_test.txt exists.
Verify that the file contains the expected content written from the NFS client.

tasks.title: Modify and Verify a File Across the NFS Share
steps: From the NFS client, modify /mnt/nfs_share/server_test.txt by adding the following line:
This file was modified from the NFS client to verify shared filesystem access.
Then, on the NFS server, verify that the changes are visible in /nfs_share/server_test.txt.

completion_message: Excellent work! You have completed Lab 229 and practiced NFS server and client configuration, NFS exports, exportfs, firewall configuration, client discovery, manual NFS mounting, read/write testing, /etc/fstab configuration, persistent NFS mounts, and NFS verification from both the server and client.
